filters.semantic_query: A named compound or nutrient was transported into brain or taken up by blood-brain barrier endothelial cells through a specific influx carrier, with uptake, inhibition, competition, saturation, kinetic, or transporter-substrate evidence.

A named ligand, conjugate, antibody, peptide, nanoparticle cargo, or therapeutic was internalized by brain endothelial cells and carried across the blood-brain barrier by receptor-mediated endocytosis or transcytosis.

A named molecule showed saturable, competitive, stereoselective, trans-stimulated, or energy-independent carrier-mediated uptake into brain or cultured brain capillary endothelial cells even though the molecular identity of the influx carrier was unknown.

Brain uptake of the named compound was saturable, competitively inhibited, stereoselective, trans-stimulated, sodium-dependent, energy-dependent, or described by Michaelis-Menten kinetics, demonstrating carrier-mediated influx across the blood-brain barrier or uptake into brain capillary endothelial cells.
